metadata.notes: agent_supports: yes (copilot has a first-class READ permission kind and a URL permission kind, both raised through the same permission.requested line as the shell/write gate 2-19 already records); daemon_capability: full (parsePermissionRequested is KIND-AGNOSTIC — it reads only requestId — and openPermissions is a set, so two sequential gates produce two distinct waiting episodes); driver_capability: ready (send/sleep/keys/wait_turn all in DRIVE_ELICITS; COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL already drops --allow-all AND disables wait_turn's auto-dismiss)

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: **yes** — GitHub Copilot CLI gates READ-ONLY work as a first-class permission kind, not as a special case of the shell gate.
daemon_capability: **full** — and for a structural reason: irrlicht's copilot parser never looks at the permission KIND, so a read-only gate is indistinguishable from the mutating gate that `2-19 tool-gate-permission-prompt` already records green.
driver_capability: **ready** — the recipe needs `send`, `sleep`, `keys`, `wait_turn`, all four in `DRIVE_ELICITS`, and the one launch lever it depends on (`COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL`) is already implemented.

## Why Copilot is the right column for this row

The row exists because of #1861, where Claude Code's permission gate reached the daemon for nine named tools and for no others — the subscriber keyed on a tool-name allowlist. Copilot's shape is the opposite, and that is the whole finding here: **the tool name never enters the picture on either side.**

### Agent — a read is its own permission kind, in the shipped schema

The CLI ships its own event schema, `schemas/session-events.schema.json` (584 KB, next to `app.js` in `@github/copilot-darwin-arm64`). `PermissionRequest` is an `anyOf` of ten members, and read-only work has three of them:

| member | schema description |
|---|---|
| `PermissionRequestRead` (`kind:"read"`) | "File or directory read permission request" |
| `PermissionRequestUrl` (`kind:"url"`) | "URL access permission request" |
| `PermissionPromptRequestPath` (`kind:"path"`) | "Path access permission prompt", with `accessKind` an enum of exactly `read` \| `shell` \| `write` — `read` documented as "Read access to a filesystem path." |

And the product documents the boundary that raises them, in its own `--help`:

> "By default, file access is restricted to paths within the current working directory and its subdirectories, plus the system temporary directory. The `--allow-all-paths` flag disables this verification…"

The TUI half is equally explicit. `app.js`'s path-permission component branches on the access kind — `let s = t==="read" ? "read" : t==="write" ? "write" : "read or write"` — and renders the dialog titled **"Allow directory access"** with the body *"This action may read the following path outside your allowed directory list."* A dialog whose copy says **read** is not a mutating gate wearing a disguise.

The URL kind is the second read-only path and is unconditional: `web_fetch` is registered as

    permissions.request({kind:"url", toolCallId, intention:"Fetch web content", url, …})

and throws outright if permissions are disabled. `--allow-all-urls` ("Allow access to all URLs without confirmation") is the flag that suppresses it, which is the documented statement that without it, it prompts.

### The emission chain — read at every seam, not inferred

The native core dispatches a prompt through one host effect, and all three branches land in the SAME emitter:

    case "permissions_request_prompt": switch (n.promptKind) {
      case "tool": return await this.requestToolPermissionFromUser(n.request, o);
      case "path": return await this.requestPathPermissionFromUser(n.request, o);
      case "url":  return await this.requestUrlPermissionFromUser(n.request, o);
    }

Each of the three calls `this.pendingRequests.requestPermissionPrompt(…)`, whose body is

    async requestPermissionPrompt(e,n){ let r=this.nativeRequest("permissionPrompt",{…}); … ; mg(this.emit, r.event); return o }

`this.emit` — **not** `this.emitEphemeral`. That distinction is the load-bearing one in this whole package (see the sibling 2-27 cell, where every other blocking-request family takes the ephemeral branch and is therefore never written to disk), and the schema states the consequence in the type itself: `PermissionRequestedEvent.ephemeral` is a plain optional boolean, whereas `ElicitationRequestedEvent.ephemeral` is `"const": true` with the description *"Always true for events that are transient and not persisted to the session event log on disk."*

So a read-only gate writes an ordinary `permission.requested` line into `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl` while the CLI sits blocked — the exact property live-verified for the shell gate on 1.0.77 in `2-19`.

### Daemon — the parser cannot tell the two classes apart, which is the point

    func parsePermissionRequested(data map[string]any, ev *tailer.ParsedEvent) {
        ev.EventType = "permission_requested"
        if id := str(data, "requestId"); id != "" { ev.PermissionRequestIDs = []string{id} }
    }

(`core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/parser.go`.) It reads `requestId` and nothing else — no `kind`, no `toolName`, no allowlist. `parsePermissionCompleted` is its mirror. There is no tool-name set anywhere on this adapter's path, so the #1861 failure mode has no place to live.

The fold is a SET, which is what makes the row's *two distinct episodes* assertion fall out rather than needing anything new:

    for _, id := range parsed.PermissionRequestIDs { t.openPermissions[id] = struct{}{} }
    for _, id := range parsed.PermissionResolvedIDs { delete(t.openPermissions, id) }

(`core/pkg/tailer/tailer.go`, `applyPermissionDeltas`.) Two sequential request/complete pairs open and close the set twice, so `TranscriptPermissionPending` (`tailer_metrics.go:656`) goes true → false → true → false, and the classifier's `transcript_permission_prompt` rule (`state_classifier.go:152`, TierTranscript → waiting) produces two separate waiting episodes. `MergeMetrics` carries the flag (`core/domain/session/metrics.go:686` — the #1256 live-path fix that `2-19`'s re-record proved), and `replayengine/metrics.go:176` carries it too, so this cell is reproducible OFFLINE like its sibling and unlike the hook-driven claudecode/codex ones.

No hook is involved in the verdict. Copilot's `notification` hook does fire for these — the native core's `permissions_notify_prompt_shown` effect calls `notifyPermissionPrompt(message)` → `fireNotificationHook(msg, "permission_prompt", "Permission needed")` for path and url prompts exactly as for shell — but irrlicht's receiver treats Notification as DISPATCH ONLY (`hooks.go`: no `session.HookSignal` row, so no hold), and it merely removes observation lag. The waiting verdict is transcript-borne end to end.

### Driver

`driver_step_types_from_file replaydata/agents/copilot/driver-interactive.sh` reports `send slash sleep wait_turn exit_clean sigkill interrupt keys restart start_session session reset_session resume`. The recipe uses four of them. Two driver facts make this cell recordable without any porting:

- `COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL=1` drops `--allow-all` from the launch line (`args+=(--allow-all)` is guarded on it), so neither `--allow-all-paths` nor `--allow-all-tools` is in effect.
- The SAME lever disables `wait_turn`'s `dismiss_dialog_if_visible "$SESSION" 'Allow|Do you want to|trust the files'`. Without that guard the driver would silently answer both dialogs within ~1 s and collapse the two episodes the cell exists to distinguish — and note the regex would match the read dialog too ("Allow directory access" / "Do you want to allow this?").

A `keys` step on this driver is spelled `{"type":"keys","text":"Enter"}` (it reads `.text`, not `.keys` — `tmux send-keys -t "$SESSION" "$(jq -r '.text' <<<"$step")"`), which is why this recipe does not copy claudecode's `"keys":"Enter"` spelling verbatim.

## What keeps this at 0.85 rather than higher

Everything above about the DAEMON is read at the seam and is kind-agnostic, so it cannot be wrong for a read-only gate unless it is also wrong for the shell gate that records green today. What is provisional is EMISSION: no recording on this host has yet captured a `permission.requested` whose kind is anything but `shell` (census: 2 in `replaydata/agents/copilot/**/transcript.jsonl`, 1 in `~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl`, all `kind:"shell"`). That the read gate fires in practice rests on the shipped schema, the CLI's own help text and the TUI component — strong primary sources, but not a live capture. Per the observation-vs-emission rule this stays provisional until `record` promotes it.
caveats: VACUOUS-PASS CONDITION (the reason this cell has a proof-of-gate step): the cell passes while proving nothing if the READ-ONLY half is never gated. A session in which the read target happens to sit inside the allowed directory list produces exactly ONE permission.requested and ONE waiting episode — which is byte-for-byte what 'the daemon merged or missed the second gate' would also produce, so the recording could not tell the two apart. The guard is POSITIVE and transcript-level, not an absence: the recorded events.jsonl must contain TWO permission.requested lines with DISTINCT requestIds, and the second must carry a read-only descriptor (permissionRequest.kind in {read, url}, or promptRequest.kind == path with accessKind in {read, shell}) with no write signal (no hasWriteFileRedirection:true, kind != write). One line, or two lines that are both write-class, means the run is INCONCLUSIVE — never a pass, and never evidence about the daemon.

LOAD-BEARING ENVIRONMENT PROPERTIES, to be RE-PROBED at record time and logged, never trusted: (1) COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL=1 must be exported — with --allow-all (= --allow-all-tools --allow-all-paths --allow-all-urls) nothing prompts at all and the cell degrades into a duplicate of 2-2; (2) the read target must lie outside the run cwd AND outside the system temporary directory, because copilot --help states those two are allowed by default (a $STAGING under /tmp makes every /tmp path pre-approved — this is the trap, since staging usually IS under the system temp dir); (3) no --add-dir on the launch line; (4) the seeded COPILOT_HOME/config.json must carry no readonlyPaths / readwritePaths / allow-rule entry covering the read target, and the recorded transcript must show NO session.permissions_changed turning allowAllPermissions on.

COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS MUST NOT BE SET for this cell, and that is a recipe input rather than operator memory. The documented cost saver COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS=bash is forwarded by the driver as --available-tools=bash, which would remove the file-read tool (and web_fetch) from the roster outright — the read-only half could then only be attempted through bash, and the run would starve rather than fail loudly. The recipe therefore pays full input-token cost on purpose; record should log the exported environment.

AN INTERMEDIATE `ready` BETWEEN THE TWO GATES IS EXPECTED and is NOT a scenario violation. Copilot closes a turn after EVERY tool call (parser.go's evTurnStart comment; 2-11's caveat measured two assistant.turn_end per prompt when a tool is involved), so after gate 1 is approved the arc is waiting → working → (tool) → ready → working → waiting rather than the row's literal waiting → working → waiting. The row's acceptance criteria are about the two episodes being DISTINCT and each being its own, which this shape satisfies more strongly than a merged one would; the spec's phases are anchored so the extra ready cannot break them. If a recording instead shows ONE merged waiting episode, the scenario is explicit that it does NOT satisfy the row — re-drive as two separate turns (write in turn 1, read in turn 2) and say so.

DIALOG DEFAULT SELECTIONS (what a bare Enter does), read from app.js: the shell/tool dialog's item list is [{label:"Yes", value:{kind:"approve-once"}}, …] with no initialItem, so index 0 is preselected and Enter approves ONCE. The path dialog (title "Allow directory access") sets initialItem to "Yes, and add these directories to the allowed list" (approve-for-session), so Enter there approves the whole directory for the rest of the session. That is harmless for this recipe (one read), but a future cell that gates TWO reads under the same directory must move the selection to the plain "Yes" first, or the second read will not prompt.

PROVISIONAL ON EMISSION, per the observation-vs-emission rule: daemon=full is derived from a kind-agnostic parser plus a live-proven shell gate, but no recording anywhere on this host yet contains a permission.requested with kind read / url / path. A census of every copilot transcript in replaydata/ (2 hits) and every live ~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl (1 hit) found kind:"shell" only. record is what promotes this from provisional to settled; if the read gate turns out not to fire, that is an AGENT finding, not a daemon one, and the fallback below is the next thing to try.

FALLBACK READ-ONLY TRIGGER, if the outside-path read does not raise a prompt: a web_fetch of any URL, with --allow-all-urls absent. app.js registers web_fetch as permissions.request({kind:"url", intention:"Fetch web content", url}) and throws if permissions are disabled, so the gate is unconditional rather than allowlist-dependent; it needs no seeded fixture but does need network egress, and its dialog's default selection was not read out of the binary (press the explicit approve item rather than a bare Enter). A code search (the ripgrep bridge also routes through permissions.request) is the second fallback. Do NOT substitute a second mutating call — that is the one substitution this row forbids.

The MUTATING half deliberately reuses 2-19's live-proven shape (a shell command with a write redirection: kind:"shell", hasWriteFileRedirection:true, gated on 1.0.77 in two separate recordings) rather than varying it the way the claudecode sibling does. claudecode varied its mutating tool because its matcher is a tool-NAME allowlist and coverage differs per name; copilot's path is kind-agnostic, so varying the mutating half would buy nothing and would trade a proven trigger for an unproven one.

sources.note: parsePermissionRequested / parsePermissionCompleted read ONLY requestId — no kind, no tool name, no allowlist. This is why a read-only gate is observationally identical to the shell gate 2-19 records green, and why #1861's tool-name-allowlist failure mode has nowhere to live on this adapter.

applyPermissionDeltas folds request ids into openPermissions (a SET) and deletes resolved ids. Two sequential request/complete pairs therefore open and close it twice — which is exactly the row's 'two distinct waiting episodes' assertion, with no new daemon behaviour required.
Line 656: TranscriptPermissionPending = len(t.openPermissions) > 0 — the derived metric the classifier reads.

Line 686: MergeMetrics copies TranscriptPermissionPending. This is the #1256 live-path fix; without it the live detector classified against a post-merge metrics struct where the flag was always false (replay was immune). 2-19's re-record is the live proof it holds.
Line 152: rule transcript_permission_prompt, TierTranscript, when m.TranscriptPermissionPending → waiting. The single rung both waiting episodes come from.

Line 176 carries TranscriptPermissionPending through the replay projection, so both waiting episodes are reconstructible offline from the frozen events.jsonl — unlike the hook-driven claudecode/codex siblings of this row.

Copilot CLI 1.0.78's own shipped event schema. PermissionRequest is an anyOf including PermissionRequestRead ('File or directory read permission request') and PermissionRequestUrl ('URL access permission request'); PermissionPromptRequestPathAccessKind is enum [read, shell, write] with read = 'Read access to a filesystem path.'. Crucially PermissionRequestedEvent.ephemeral is a PLAIN optional boolean, while ElicitationRequestedEvent.ephemeral is const:true described as 'Always true for events that are transient and not persisted to the session event log on disk' — i.e. the schema itself states that permission.requested IS persisted.

CLI 1.0.78 bundle. (a) Native host effect 'permissions_request_prompt' routes promptKind tool|path|url into requestToolPermissionFromUser / requestPathPermissionFromUser / requestUrlPermissionFromUser. (b) All three call PendingRequests.requestPermissionPrompt, whose body ends `mg(this.emit, r.event)` — the NON-ephemeral emitter (contrast requestUserInput / requestElicitation / requestExitPlanMode, which all use mg(this.emitEphemeral, …)). (c) The path dialog component: `s = t==="read" ? "read" : t==="write" ? "write" : "read or write"`, title "Allow directory access", body "This action may read the following path outside your allowed directory list.", initialItem = 'Yes, and add these directories to the allowed list'. (d) web_fetch registers permissions.request({kind:"url", intention:"Fetch web content", url}) and throws when permissions are disabled. (e) permissions_notify_prompt_shown → notifyPermissionPrompt → fireNotificationHook(msg, "permission_prompt", "Permission needed"), so the notification hook fires for path/url prompts too.

'Path Permissions: By default, file access is restricted to paths within the current working directory and its subdirectories, plus the system temporary directory. The --allow-all-paths flag disables this verification and allows access to any path on the filesystem.' Also --allow-all-urls ('Allow access to all URLs without confirmation') and --allow-all ('equivalent to --allow-all-tools --allow-all-paths --allow-all-urls'). This is the documented boundary the read-only half is driven across, and the documented reason --allow-all must be off.

handleNotificationHook accepts permission_prompt and elicitation_dialog but is DISPATCH ONLY — session.HookSignal has no Notification row, so no hold is taken and only a synthetic activity event is injected. Confirms the waiting verdict here is transcript-borne, and that a hook failure could at worst add latency, not remove an episode.

DRIVE_ELICITS lists send/slash/sleep/wait_turn/keys/... — every step this recipe needs. `[[ -z "${COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL:-}" ]] && args+=(--allow-all)` is the launch lever, and the SAME variable guards wait_turn's dismiss_dialog_if_visible 'Allow|Do you want to|trust the files' — a regex that would otherwise auto-answer BOTH dialogs (it matches the read dialog's 'Allow directory access' / 'Do you want to allow this?' too). The keys arm reads .text, not .keys.

The mutating half, live-proven: CLI 1.0.77 sitting blocked with permission.requested {kind:"shell", hasWriteFileRedirection:true} already on disk, and the daemon emitting state_transition→waiting with decided_by_rule=transcript_permission_prompt after the MergeMetrics fix. This cell's first gate reuses that exact trigger.

The baseline this row is measured against: under COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL, `cat data.txt` / `ls -la` inside the cwd auto-approve with NO permission.requested at all, while `echo written > out.txt` gates. That is what makes 'read-only inside the workspace' the wrong trigger for this row and 'read-only OUTSIDE the allowed directory list' the right one — and it is the source of the vacuous-pass discipline this cell copies.

The report the row was written from (Claude Code: the permission gate reached the daemon for nine named tools and no others). Cited here as the row's provenance and as the contrast case — copilot's subscriber path names no tools at all.

preconditions: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.78+ on PATH and authenticated (credentials live in the OS keychain, so COPILOT_HOME isolation needs no re-login). Assessed against 1.0.78.

An active Copilot plan with AI credits — this recipe spends one multi-tool turn. Do NOT record over BYOK: totalNanoAiu is 0 and the BYOK model name falls outside irrlicht's priced alias map, so the cost observation would land at zero.

COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL=1 MUST be exported. It drops --allow-all from the driver's launch line (so --allow-all-paths and --allow-all-tools are both off) AND disables wait_turn's dismiss_dialog_if_visible, which would otherwise answer both dialogs within ~1s and collapse the two episodes. The lever already exists in the driver; nothing needs porting.

COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS MUST NOT be set for this cell — the driver forwards it as --available-tools, which would remove the file-read tool and web_fetch from the roster and starve the read-only half. This cell deliberately pays full input-token cost.

RE-PROBE AT RECORD TIME, and log what was found: (a) the seeded read target is outside the run cwd and outside the system temporary directory (copilot --help: those two are allowed by default — if $STAGING is under /tmp, every /tmp path is pre-approved); (b) no --add-dir is on the launch line; (c) the seeded COPILOT_HOME/config.json carries no readonlyPaths / readwritePaths / allow-rule entry covering the target.
irrlicht's copilot `transcripts` permission granted (IRRLICHT_PERMISSION_MODE=grant-all for the recorder) — a fresh IRRLICHT_HOME leaves it pending and the daemon observes nothing.

No hook install and no :7837 pinning needed — the whole signal is transcript-borne, so the :7838 coexist recorder captures it. (The copilot notification hook, if installed, only removes observation lag; it takes no hold.)
tmux available (the interactive driver drives the REPL through it).
setup: The driver isolates state under $STAGING/copilot-home via COPILOT_HOME and seeds trustedFolders + askedSetupTerminals so neither first-run modal blocks the input box, then waits for the '/ commands' footer before typing. A fresh per-run cwd is created under $STAGING/cwd/.

SEED THE READ TARGET OUTSIDE THE ALLOWED LIST: create $HOME/.irrlicht-onboard/copilot-2-26/outside.txt containing the single line OUTSIDE-OK. $HOME is neither the run cwd nor the system temporary directory, which is what makes the read cross copilot's default path-verification boundary. Record the absolute path it used into the run log — the prompt below must name that exact absolute path.

ASSERT BEFORE DRIVING (fail loudly, do not proceed on a guess): the seeded path is not under the run cwd, not under $TMPDIR / /tmp / /private/tmp, and does not appear in $COPILOT_HOME/config.json. If any of those is false, the read half is pre-approved and the run would be vacuous.
Confirm out.txt does NOT already exist in the run cwd, so the write half is a real create.

The recipe answers BOTH dialogs deliberately with `keys` steps. wait_turn must not be used while either dialog is held — under COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL it no longer auto-dismisses, but it would still return early on copilot's first assistant.turn_end.

script.text:
Do exactly these two steps, in this order, one at a time. Wait for each step to finish completely before starting the next one. Do not use any tool other than the two named here.
Step 1: use the bash tool to run exactly this command: echo written > out.txt
Step 2: use your file-reading tool (not bash) to read the file at the absolute path <ABSOLUTE_OUTSIDE_PATH> and report the single line it contains.
When both steps are done, reply with exactly one line containing only: BOTH-DONE

verify: PROOF OF TWO GATES (must fail loudly; absence of a finding and inability to look must not produce the same output): the recorded transcript contains EXACTLY TWO permission.requested lines with DISTINCT requestId values, each followed by a permission.completed carrying the same requestId. Fewer than two means the run is INCONCLUSIVE — report it as such and do not grade the phases.

PROOF THE SECOND GATE IS READ-ONLY: the second permission.requested carries a read-only descriptor — permissionRequest.kind in {read, url}, or promptRequest.kind == "path" with accessKind in {read, shell} — and carries NO write signal (kind != write, hasWriteFileRedirection not true). Record the exact kind/accessKind observed into the cell's caveats: this is the first non-shell permission kind any copilot recording will have captured.
PROOF THE FIRST GATE IS MUTATING: the first permission.requested carries kind:"shell" with hasWriteFileRedirection:true and possiblePaths containing out.txt (the 2-19 shape).

PROOF THE LAUNCH CONFIG WAS HONOURED: the recorded transcript contains NO session.permissions_changed turning allowAllPermissions on. Its presence means COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL was not honoured and the cell is vacuous whatever the pass rate says.

events.jsonl contains a presession_created (proc-<PID>) in ready shortly after launch, then a transcript_new for the real session (the ~/.copilot/session-state/<dir> name — a DIFFERENT id) born DIRECTLY into working, plus a pid_discovered bound to the real session.

THE ASSERTION UNDER TEST: events.jsonl shows TWO distinct state_transition→waiting for the real session with at least one state_transition→working between them — one bound to the shell write gate, one to the read gate. A single waiting episode does NOT satisfy this row.
The session is back at ready after the second approval and STILL ready across the >=10s trailing idle (no state_transition to waiting in that window).
The final assistant message contains the literal token BOTH-DONE and the transcript shows out.txt created, proving both gated calls actually executed after approval rather than being cancelled.
